citations.review_text:
Killing Floor is one of those games I wish I had played sooner. It’s a co-op survival horror FPS from Tripwire Interactive that originally released in 2009, and even though it’s an older game, I actually had a pretty good time with it.

The main thing I like about Killing Floor is how simple the idea is. You’re basically fighting through waves of enemies, getting better weapons and equipment as you go, and trying to survive until the final boss. You can play by yourself, but the game is really designed around co-op, with up to six players working together.

I also really like the different classes, or Perks, because they give you different ways to play. You can specialize in things like healing, support, explosives, or different types of weapons. It gives you a reason to keep playing and leveling up your character.

The weapons are also pretty fun. There are a lot of different weapons to use, and shooting the enemies feels satisfying. The enemies can get pretty crazy too, especially when you start getting into the harder waves. The game can go from being manageable to completely chaotic really quickly.

One thing I wasn't expecting was how much content there actually is. There are a ton of maps, weapons, achievements, and community content, and Steam currently lists 285 achievements for the game.

The graphics definitely show the game's age, though. This is a 2009 game, and you can tell. Some of the character models, environments, and animations look pretty dated compared with newer games. But honestly, I don't think that takes away too much from the experience.

I also like that Killing Floor doesn't try to be something it isn't. It's mainly about jumping into a game, shooting monsters, surviving waves, and having fun. There's a story and a setting behind everything, but the gameplay is definitely the main focus.

Overall, I enjoyed Killing Floor. It's an older game, but it still has a lot of fun gameplay, especially if you have friends to play with. …

[b]Introduction :[/b]
Killing Floor est un FPS coopératif développé par Tripwire Interactive, sorti en 2009 après avoir débuté comme simple mod d'Unreal Tournament 2004. Le concept est simple : survivre en équipe à des vagues de Zeds, des mutants répugnants, avant d'affronter le Patriarch en boss final.

[b]Ce que j'ai aimé :[/b]
[list]
[*]🧟 L'ambiance crade et poisseuse qui donne au jeu une vraie identité, bien loin des shooters aseptisés
[*]🎯 Le Zed Time, ce bullet-time collectif qui rend chaque headshot absolument jouissif
[*]🤝 La coop à 6 qui fonctionne à merveille, avec un système de classes (perks) qui pousse à jouer en équipe
[*]🔫 Une grande variété d'armes, du fusil à pompe à la tronçonneuse, chacune avec son feeling propre
[*]💰 Un petit prix et des années de contenu gratuit ajouté par Tripwire, le rapport qualité/prix est imbattable
[/list]

[b]Ce que j'ai moins aimé :[/b]
[list]
[*]🖼️ Des graphismes datés qui trahissent ses origines de mod, même pour 2009
[*]🔁 Une boucle de gameplay répétitive : on tourne en rond dans des maps fermées en tuant les mêmes monstres
[*]👾 Un bestiaire limité qui montre vite ses limites sur la durée
[/list]

[b]Conclusion :[/b]
Killing Floor, c'est l'alternative gore et décomplexée à Left 4 Dead. Moins beau, plus répétitif, mais tellement efficace en coop entre potes. Le Zed Time et le système de perks suffisent à eux seuls à justifier l'achat, surtout vu le prix. Un classique du FPS coopératif qui a lancé toute une franchise. Recommandé.

[b]Note :[/b] ★★★★☆

claims.claim: The core gameplay loop and wave-based survival mechanics become repetitive after playing for a while.

citations.review_text: Killing Floor was an amazing game and I had a great time with it. The gameplay is fun and satisfying it definitely starts to get repetitive after playing for a while. It's also a much better experience when you have friends to play with, but even solo it's still a great game. Overall, despite the repetition, I really enjoyed my time with it and would recommend it, especially if you have friends to jump in with.

Killing Floor is a cooperative survival horror shooter developed by Tripwire Interactive. Originally released as a mod before becoming a standalone game, it quickly gained popularity thanks to its intense gameplay and challenging cooperative experience.

The game takes place in a world overrun by terrifying mutant creatures known as Zeds. Players must work together to survive multiple waves of enemies, earn money, and purchase better weapons between rounds. Teamwork is essential, especially on higher difficulty levels where a single mistake can lead to disaster.

One of the strongest aspects of Killing Floor is its weapon system. Players can choose from a wide range of firearms and explosives, each with its own strengths and weaknesses. The game also features different classes, known as Perks, which allow players to specialize in areas such as healing, sharpshooting, or demolition.

The atmosphere is darker and more horror-focused than many modern shooters. Dimly lit environments, disturbing enemy designs, and tense music create a constant feeling of danger. Every wave becomes more difficult, keeping players under pressure throughout the match.

Although the graphics are outdated by modern standards, they still fit the game's horror theme well. The gameplay remains fun and satisfying, especially when playing with friends.

The main drawback is that the game can become repetitive after many hours, as the objective is always to survive waves of enemies. New players may also find the difficulty challenging at first.

Overall, Killing Floor is a classic cooperative shooter that successfully combines horror and action. Its challenging gameplay, unique atmosphere, and strong teamwork mechanics make it a memorable experience for fans of survival games.

Rating: 8/10

Killing Floor is a really good game and an absolute blast to play, especially with friends. One of its strongest aspects is the RPG style progression system, where you level up different perks to improve your class. Each perk enhances a specific playstyle, unlocking bonuses like increased damage, better survivability, faster reloads, or special abilities that make your role in the team feel meaningful and rewarding.

This progression system adds depth and long term motivation, encouraging you to experiment with different classes and find the one that fits your playstyle best. Combined with the intense, fast paced combat and strong emphasis on teamwork, the perk system makes every match feel impactful. If you enjoy co-op shooters with RPG progression and class customization, Killing Floor is definitely recommended, especially with friends.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game features a dark, grimy atmosphere and varied indoor and outdoor map designs.

citations.review_text: The grimy atmosphere in Killing Floor 1 was peak. I was disappointed that KF2 never managed to capture that same feeling.

Enough summer months spent and more scattered around the year that I'll probably never forget my time in this.
The normal game alone was tons of fun. I loved the variety of indoor, outdoor, night and day maps. 
I miss spamming Insult Players with friends and randoms, and the excessive amount of bri'ish never failed to make me laugh, especially when people were running for their lives.
The custom servers were amazing, and that's where I simply couldn't leave. 
Unfortunately, all of the ones I used to play on are all gone, but I'll always remember them.

This game will always be one of the ones I look back at fondly. v23
